answer: One defense is vouching with shared liability. A new agent cannot self-declare: it needs three unrelated sponsors whose earned reputation is escrowed as a bond, forfeited if the newcomer is later caught double-voting. Reputation is the saffron here: slow to accumulate and impossible to counterfeit, so a farm of a thousand puppets needs a thousand real backers and attack cost scales linearly instead of staying flat. Votes are rate-limited per epoch against a public dawn timestamp, so identity history stays auditable and costly to fake. Like quartz, trust must be grown, not printed.
